issues.description: trainer_args key mismatch: docstring documents max_steps/val_interval but code reads max_step and never honors val_interval
issues.detail: The constructor docstring promises keys max_steps, log_interval, val_interval, save_interval, but __init__ reads trainer_args['max_step'] (singular) and validation runs every save_interval. Callers writing configs to the documented contract will KeyError on launch or get the wrong cadence. Reconcile names, honor val_interval, and assert required keys at __init__.

issues.description: Checkpoint discovery is fragile: name-based sort with no atomicity guard and brittle int() parse
issues.detail: load_checkpoint filters any directory containing 'step_' and parses int(name.split('step_')[-1]), which crashes on names like 'step_100_backup' and silently resumes from half-written directories after a mid-save crash. Tighten the predicate (startswith('step_') or regex) and write a 'latest' marker on successful save so resume verifies completeness.

issues.description: run() training loop has no inner max_step check; overshoots or mis-saves at boundary
issues.detail: The outer while loop advances global_step by save_interval inside train() with no inner check, so it overshoots max_step by up to save_interval-1 when the interval does not divide evenly. On resume at exactly max_step the loop exits without saving final state. State the loop invariant and enforce the bound inside train().

issues.description: _all_reduce_stats has confusing ownership: mutates tensors in place and also rebinds dict entries, with no key-set consistency check across ranks
issues.detail: The function divides tensors in place then reassigns stats[key] = stats[key] / world_size, so callers holding the original tensor see partial mutation. Worse, SUM/world_size is only a correct mean if every rank contributes every key; a missing key on one rank silently produces wrong values. Make the contract pure or destructive (not both) and assert key alignment.

issues.description: valid_*_specifier parsing uses whitespace split with no grammar validation, despite paths embedded in tokens
issues.detail: train.py calls .split() on valid specifiers whose documented format is 'task:name:data_json[:factor]' where data_json is a path that may contain spaces. The grammar lives only in --help text with no parser. One space in a path produces two bogus specs keyed by raw strings. Lift the grammar into a small typed parser and validate at startup.

issues.description: _load_checkpoint silently falls through when an explicit resume_path is missing
issues.detail: If the caller passes a resume_path that does not exist, the code falls through to 'start from step 0' rather than raising. A user expecting to resume a long training run will silently retrain from scratch and only notice hours later. Raise FileNotFoundError when resume_path is explicit and missing; only fall through when no resume was requested.

synthesis.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The panel converges on three blocking correctness issues: a docstring/code key mismatch (max_steps vs max_step, plus an unused val_interval) that will KeyError or mis-schedule on first run; checkpoint discovery that parses directory names fragilely with no atomicity guard against half-written saves; and a training loop with no stated max_step invariant that overshoots or skips the final save. Secondary but worth fixing before this becomes a long-lived module boundary: _all_reduce_stats has confusing ownership and an unchecked cross-rank key precondition, the valid specifier parser whitespace-splits path-bearing tokens with no grammar validation, and _load_checkpoint silently retrains from scratch when an explicit resume_path is missing.
